correctness.rationale: For squarefree p<q<r<s the equation is the exact product identity H(p)H(q)H(r)H(s)=2 with H decreasing. Successive strict upper bounds reduce p to 5 or 7, reduce q to four pairs, and reduce r to fifteen exact triples. The fourth prime is then uniquely s=(2+A)/(2-A). Exact rational evaluation leaves eight prime outputs and rejects every other triple. The attached verifier independently replays these bounds and validates all eight equations.

value.rationale: Four distinct primes are the first squarefree support layer immediately beyond the published exact support-at-most-three theorem. The 2014 sequel treats larger supports by heuristic examples, so an exact support-four classification is a natural next structural question. The eight-element theorem is unbounded, explains a conspicuous block of the exact database, and is obtained by a reusable monotone factor-reduction method rather than by a numerical cutoff.
